This allows $O(1)$ retrieval of the sum of $\tau$ over any axis-aligned bounding box [S1, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly states that the aggregation operation (summing extinction coefficients) is implemented using a 3D Summed Area Table (SAT). It further notes that 'With a 3D SAT it is possible to derive the sum of all elements in...' a region. In computer graphics and data structures, a fundamental property of a Summed Area Table (also known as a Integral Image/Table) is that it allows for the calculation of the sum of values within any axis-aligned rectangular region (or bounding box in 3D) in constant time, O(1), regardless of the size of the region. The claim accurately reflects the computational advantage and mechanism described in the source.
